description:
FILED s415, found while clearing #401's first blocker.

perl builds an interpolated string with the CONCATENATION operator, so an
overloaded `.` participates and the result need not be a string at all:

    package o { use overload "." => sub { $_[0] }, fallback => 1 }
    our $o = bless [], "o";
    my $cat = "a $o b";
    print ref($cat), "\n";      # perl: o      PCL: (empty)

PCL stringifies the interpolated pieces instead (`to-string` on the box), so
the overload never runs and the result is always a plain string.  This is
[perl #124160], and t/opbasic/concat.t:203 is a test row for exactly it:

    ok(ref(CORE::state $y = "a $o b") eq 'o',
       'state $y = "foo $bar baz" does not stringify; only concats');

That row now RUNS and FAILS honestly (before s415 the file did not transpile at
all).  Nothing else in either population depends on it.

WHERE: the interpolation lowering builds `(p-string-concat â¦)` over
already-stringified pieces.  The fix is to make the interpolation concat go
through the SAME overload-aware path a source-level `.` takes (`p-.`), at least
when a piece can be an object.  Note the asymmetry to preserve: only `.` is
consulted, not `""` â an object with a `""` overload but no `.` stringifies as
usual, which is what fallback does.

RELATED: #119 (s///&m// match-source stringification skips overload) is the
same family â a stringify-instead-of-overload shortcut â and the two should be
looked at together.


DONE s419d (79702aa): RUNTIME-ONLY -- p-string-concat folds left through p-. when a piece registers a . handler (emission already passes pieces raw; no gen bump).  perl multiconcat semantics probed first (one call per object piece, reversed flag, plain result ends dispatch, single piece stringifies); all rows byte-identical.  t/opbasic/concat.t 248/6 -> 249/5, the [perl #124160] row -- the only change-attributed companion mover.  Guard Pl/t/overload-01.t.
subject: String interpolation stringifies instead of CONCATENATING: an overloaded `.` never runs, so ref("a $obj b") is empty where perl says the class ([perl #124160], concat.t:203)
